summary: Composio does not provide a managed DocuSign OAuth app, so you must create an integration key (your OAuth client) in a free DocuSign developer (demo) account and give Composio the key and secret. The demo flow works in under an hour. Production is the hard part. The key has to pass DocuSign's automated "go-live" review (historically, your 20 most recent API calls in demo must succeed with no errors and no polling). It then gets promoted into a paid production DocuSign account (not a trial) where you are an admin. Biggest gotcha: demo keys and secrets only work against account-d.docusign.com. Until the key is promoted and you create a new production secret, real users on account.docusign.com cannot connect.

verdict.difficultyReason: Setting up in demo is self-serve and free, but before any real user can connect you need an automated go-live review and a paid, non-trial DocuSign production account where you are an admin.

devReady.detail: Works in the DocuSign demo environment (account-d.docusign.com) with your free developer account. You can also connect any other demo-environment account. Envelopes are not legally binding, and real production users cannot sign in with this key yet.

productionReady.estimate: 1-3 days if you already have a paid DocuSign production account; longer if you need to buy one or upgrade to an API-capable plan
productionReady.detail: Make clean API calls in demo (historically 20 straight successful, non-polling calls; login and userinfo calls don't count). Then click Go-Live / Submit for review in Apps and Keys. Reports say the automated review finishes in minutes. Then sign in as an admin of a paid, non-trial production account to promote the key, create a NEW secret key in production, re-add the redirect URI, and point Composio at production. Once that's done, users from any DocuSign account can consent to your key with authorization code grant.

verdict.handsOnEffort: 2-4 hours (plus scripting 20+ clean demo API calls)

nextAction: Sign up for a free DocuSign developer account at https://developers.docusign.com, then open https://admindemo.docusign.com/apps-and-keys and click "Add App and Integration Key".

prerequisites.detail: Free. Sign up at developers.docusign.com. You get admin access to Apps and Keys at admindemo.docusign.com.

Can't be a trial. The plan must support API integrations (third-party reports say Business Pro or higher; the error otherwise is 'These accounts don't support API integrations'). The person promoting the key must be an admin on it.

prerequisites.item: Clean API call history in demo
prerequisites.detail: Historically, your 20 most recent API calls with the key must succeed. Login/userinfo calls don't count, and you must not poll the same envelope within 15 minutes.
Needed to create a custom Auth Config with your integration key and secret
Not required by DocuSign for basic go-live (not seen in the docs we fetched), but good practice for the consent screen and any App Center listing

phases.title: Register the integration key (demo)
phases.goal: You have an integration key (client ID) and secret in the demo environment with Composio's redirect URI registered

steps.title: Create a free developer account
steps.detail: Sign up at developers.docusign.com and confirm your email. This creates a demo account on account-d.docusign.com.

steps.title: Add an app and integration key
steps.detail: Go to admindemo.docusign.com > Settings/Admin > Integrations > Apps and Keys. Click 'Add App and Integration Key', name it (e.g. '[YOUR PRODUCT] Agent'), and click Create App. Copy the Integration Key; this is your Client ID.

steps.title: Configure authorization code grant with a secret
steps.detail: Under Authentication, choose that your integration is able to keep secrets (confidential client / Authorization Code Grant). Click 'Add Secret Key' and copy it right away, because it is shown only once.

steps.title: Register Composio's redirect URI
steps.detail: Under Additional settings > Redirect URIs, click Add URI and enter exactly: https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add. Then click Save.

phases.title: Connect through Composio and test with your account
phases.goal: An OAuth flow completes with your demo account and Composio DocuSign tools run

steps.title: Create a custom Auth Config in Composio
steps.detail: In dashboard.composio.dev, go to Auth Configs > Create Auth Config > DocuSign > OAuth2. Paste the Integration Key as Client ID and the Secret Key as Client Secret. Keep the scopes 'signature' (plus 'extended' if you want long-lived refresh; 'impersonation' is only needed for JWT). Click Create and copy the ac_... ID.

steps.title: Make sure Composio targets the demo environment
steps.detail: Demo keys only work against https://account-d.docusign.com/oauth/auth and /oauth/token. If the Composio auth config has an environment or base URL field, set it to demo (account-d). Production uses account.docusign.com.

steps.title: Pass the auth config into your session
steps.detail: In your Composio session, set authConfigs: { docusign: 'ac_...' }. Start a connection, sign in with your demo account, and approve consent.

steps.title: Generate clean API traffic for go-live
steps.detail: Run at least 20 consecutive successful calls (e.g. list envelopes, create a draft envelope, list templates, get account info). Don't hit the same envelope twice within 15 minutes, and avoid any 4xx/5xx errors. Check your call history in the API Dashboard of your developer account.

phases.title: Go live and promote to production
phases.goal: The key exists in production with its own secret and the redirect URI, so any DocuSign user can connect
phases.waitTime: Reports say the automated review result appears within minutes (~20 min). Promotion is instant once you pass.

steps.title: Submit for go-live review
steps.detail: In demo Apps and Keys, open the key's Actions menu and choose Go-Live / 'Submit for review' (status changes once the call criteria are met). If it fails, fix the erroring calls and re-run 20 clean ones.

steps.title: Promote to a production account
steps.detail: Choose 'Select Go-Live account' and sign in as an admin of a paid, non-trial production account, then accept the terms. Turn off pop-up blockers first. The key is copied to production (it stays in demo too).

steps.title: Create a production secret and redirect URI
steps.detail: In admin.docusign.com > Apps and Keys, open the promoted key. Click Add Secret Key (demo secrets do not work in production) and add https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add under Redirect URIs. Then click Save.

steps.title: Switch Composio to production
steps.detail: Create a new Composio Auth Config (or update the existing one) with the same Client ID, the production secret and the production environment (account.docusign.com). After login, read the user's base_uri from /oauth/userinfo, because API hosts vary per account (na1, na2, eu, etc.).

phases.title: Ongoing maintenance
phases.goal: Connections stay healthy and within API rules

steps.title: Use Connect webhooks instead of polling
steps.detail: DocuSign enforces polling limits (no repeated requests for the same envelope within 15 minutes) and hourly API limits. Use DocuSign Connect for status triggers.

steps.title: Rotate secrets
steps.detail: You can add a second secret key before you delete the old one. Update Composio first.

scopes.reviewNote: No separate review; covered by go-live

scopes.reviewNote: No review needed; recommended so agent connections don't expire

Requires the Click product on the account plan

blockers.title: Go-live review fails on errored calls
blockers.symptom: Review fails; staff point to a 404 or other error among the last 20 calls
blockers.fix: Fix the endpoint (e.g. 'brands' not 'brand'), then re-run 20 consecutive successful, non-login calls before resubmitting

blockers.title: Polling violation
blockers.symptom: Go-live review fails even though all calls succeeded
blockers.fix: Don't request the same envelope within 15 minutes; cache results; use Connect webhooks

blockers.title: Production account not eligible
blockers.symptom: 'These accounts don't support API integrations' or a trial account can't be selected during promotion
blockers.fix: Use a paid, non-trial production account on an API-capable plan, and sign in as its admin. Contact DocuSign sales/support to upgrade

blockers.title: Demo key used against production
blockers.symptom: 'The client id provided is not registered with Docusign' when users sign in on account.docusign.com
blockers.fix: Promote the key via go-live, then use account.docusign.com endpoints with the new production secret

blockers.title: Demo secret doesn't work in production
blockers.symptom: invalid_client at the production token endpoint
blockers.fix: Create a new Secret Key in admin.docusign.com Apps and Keys and update Composio

blockers.title: Promoted key missing in production
blockers.symptom: Key doesn't show up in production Apps and Keys after go-live
blockers.fix: Check Admin > Apps and Keys in each production account you control. Open a DocuSign support case to find which account holds the key

technical.pkce: DocuSign supports PKCE for public clients (reported). Discovery metadata does not advertise code_challenge_methods. Confidential clients with a secret (as Composio uses) don't need it.
technical.refreshTokens: Access token ~8 hours (expires_in 28800). Refresh token ~30 days with the 'extended' scope; reported to roll forward as you use it. Store the new refresh token returned on each refresh.
technical.redirectUriRules: Each URI must be registered under the key's Redirect URIs and match exactly. Multiple URIs allowed. Production keys keep their own settings after promotion, so verify the URI there.
technical.notes: Two separate environments (demo account-d vs production account), with different secrets. After token exchange, call /oauth/userinfo to get the account's base_uri (e.g. https://na3.docusign.net); API host differs per account and region. Grant types in discovery: authorization_code, implicit; JWT is also supported for service integrations. Token endpoint auth: client_secret_basic or client_secret_post. No dynamic client registration advertised.

canDo: Fill out the Apps and Keys form via browser automation while you are logged in
Configure the Composio Auth Config and session authConfigs
Write and run a script that makes 20+ clean, non-polling eSignature API calls in demo for go-live
Read the API Dashboard / call logs and fix erroring calls before resubmitting
Handle base_uri lookup via /oauth/userinfo and the switch between demo and production endpoints
youMustDo: Create the DocuSign developer account and sign in
Buy or confirm a paid, non-trial production plan that supports APIs
Click Submit for review and promote the key while signed in as a production admin (accept the terms)
Copy secrets (shown once) and store them safely
Contact DocuSign support/sales if promotion or plan eligibility fails

probes.observed: Both serve /.well-known/openid-configuration. authorize /oauth/auth, token /oauth/token, grants authorization_code+implicit, auth methods client_secret_basic/post, scopes include signature, organization_read, user_write. No registration_endpoint, no PKCE methods advertised.
probes.conclusion: Endpoints confirmed for both environments. No dynamic registration, so you must create the key manually.

probes.action: Authorize request with unregistered client_id and Composio redirect URI
probes.observed: HTTP 200 'Docusign' page; no redirect back to Composio
probes.conclusion: Endpoint is live. DocuSign shows its own page (an error or login) rather than redirecting, so unregistered or mismatched redirect URIs don't leak back.

probes.action: HTTP GET of the demo console
probes.observed: 200, title 'Home Page - Intelligent Agreement Management' (login/app shell)
probes.conclusion: Console exists and requires a DocuSign login.

uncertainties: Official developers.docusign.com pages are rendered client-side and could not be fetched. Go-live criteria come from a DocuSign blog plus third-party guides.

Sources conflict on whether the '20 successful API calls' requirement still applies. Frontegg says promotion is now automatic for most integration types. Assume you need clean calls and confirm in your Apps and Keys UI.
The exact production plan tier needed (reported 'Business Pro or higher' / API plan) is not confirmed by DocuSign docs.
Whether Composio's DocuSign toolkit lets you choose demo vs production endpoints, and how it handles per-account base_uri, is unverified. Check the Auth Config fields.
Whether requesting the 'impersonation' scope in the auth-code flow causes extra consent friction is not tested.
Token lifetimes (8h access, ~30-day refresh with 'extended') come from third-party sources.
Review timing (~20 minutes) is reported, not documented.
